 Railway worker body seeks Rs 69,000 minimum wage from 8th pay commission
 SECTIONS Railway worker body seeks Rs 69,000 minimum wage from 8th pay commission By Twesh Mishra , ET Bureau Last Updated: Oct 30, 2026, 08:51:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis The National Federation of Indian Railwaymen has presented demands to the 8th Central Pay Commission. They have requested a minimum salary of Rs 69,000 for employees, along with a fitment factor of 3.833. Additionally, they seek an increase in annual increments from 3% to 6% and at least five promotions during service. The federation also wants the merger of dearness allowance with basic pay when it reaches 25%.
 Agencies The National federation of Railwaymen sought doubling the annual increment from 3% to 6%, with a minimum financial benefit of Rs 10,000, and at least five promotions during an employee’s service.
 The National Federation of Indian Railwaymen has sought a minimum pay of Rs 69,000 per employee in its representation on the 8th Central Pay Commission . The railway worker body pitched a fitment factor of 3.833 to “ensure an adequate and meaningful revision of pay.”
 According to an NFIR statement, a delegation led by president Guman Singh and general secretary M. Raghavaiah presented its demands before the commission in New Delhi on Friday.
 Read more: Railway pass holders can travel in higher class on Rajdhani, Shatabdi by paying fare difference 
The federation sought doubling the annual increment from 3% to 6% , with a minimum financial benefit of Rs 10,000, and at least five promotions during an employee’s service.
It also demanded merger of dearness allowance with basic pay whenever DA reaches 25%, open-ended pay scales and a distinct pay structure recognising the arduous and hazardous nature of railway duties.
 Live Events
On pensions, NFIR proposed 67% of last pay drawn, 50% family pension and reducing the commutation deduction period from 15 years to 11 years. Other demands included restoring discontinued allowances, tripling allowances, job-specific benefits and including parents in employees’ railway passes.
